The lifetime of the $B^0_s$ meson is evaluated using a maximum-likelihood method, yielding a direct result of $\tau(B^0_s)\times c = 459.9\pm2.6_{\rm(stat)}\pm1.3_{\rm syst}$ $\mu{\rm m}$.  This finding, based on a dataset equivalent to 3.0fb$^{-1}$ at an center-of-mass energy of 7.8 TeV, is consistent with previous measurements and theoretical predictions.

This study focuses on a specific case of a dispersing control system described by the stochastic heat equation with discrete controls, which are located at distinct spatial points. The research is conducted with reference to prior findings by Danilatos and Tournis, as well as Danilatos and Karafyllis. Building upon an existing result showing that no perfect control exists in this scenario, we establish the existence of an approximate control within a specific class of smooth functions. Furthermore, we provide the explicit form of this approximate control.

Our investigation reveals an unexpected and vast pattern in high-energy corpuscular-cray movements, which lack apparent relation to the star positions. Above 4 EeV, this surrprising finding becomes evident and can be attributed to a significant and range-dependent anisotropy in energy distribution. Specifically, we observe a notable influence of moon's position on the frequency of recorded events, which impacts nearly 40% of very high-energy corpuscles, and whose effect grows as energy increases.

The ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is capable of measuring charged particle properties and relationships between pairs of particles in p+Pb collisions, utilizing special triggers that identify forward particles with high energy and mass, detected by the calorimeters and hadron spectrometer. This study presents data collection strategies, as well as methods for evaluating and estimating uncertainty in this unique dataset. Moreover, it defines and measures various indicators of how particles behave, including their momentum, direction, spatial position, and the nuclear alteration factor. This last measure is particularly useful for understanding particle production processes. Nonetheless, certain aspects of this approach remain relative minor topics.

The study focuses on quantum dynamical systems within a noncommutative setting, specifically those connected to simple Lie groups and their associated star-products. Key properties of these systems are explored, with an emphasis on chaotic behavior and the preservation of metric characteristics. Consideration is given to systems derived from compact forms of simple Lie groups, considering various values of their deformation parameters.

In describing the spatial distribution of tumor cells and lymphocytes within histological images, the assessment of tumor infiltration lymphocytes holds significant importance for cancer patients' treatment and prognosis. However, image analysis within this domain faces a major obstacle due to the lack of expert-annotated images necessary for training deep learning models. As a means of overcoming this challenge, our study explores the potential of federated learning to train models across multiple collaborating institutions, thus avoiding the exchange of sensitive medical data. Furthermore, an evaluation of the performance of both centrally and federatively trained models was conducted through experiments, demonstrating the effectiveness of the federated approach in achieving accurate image categorization.

Researchers have developed high-speed underwater fiber-optic transmission lines that are crucial for efficient marine communications. However, the optical signals can be disrupted due to physical pressure from underwater, leading to the formation of bursts of errors that undermine the performance of equalization techniques commonly used to mitigate inter-symbol interference. To improve the robustness of equalizers, a novel approach has been proposed by inserting adaptive filters between the faulty segments of the transmission line and the equalizer. These additional filters are tailored to compensate for the pressure-induced disruptions and are optimized to enhance the decision-feedback equalizer's performance, thereby ensuring more reliable and efficient underwater fiber-optic communications.

Deep Learning techniques have gained popularity in Video Action Recognition due to their effectiveness, however, Video input often contains unnecessary parts like background and foreground, which can hinder performance, leading research experts to design optimized network architectures like TCANet and TRSNet. Although these designs have improved efficiency by reducing parameters and computational complexity, many critical layers still need to be retained for accurate action recognition. Our analysis indicates that many trimmed layers contribute little to overall performance, prompting our discovery that some network components can be optimized for better resource use. This led us to introduce a new network structure-optimization module called Trimming In Time, which removes redundant layers while maintaining good performance. Our experiments showed that Trimming In Time significantly reduces the number of parameters and FLOPs, resulting in more efficient networks with satisfactory accuracy.

It has been proven that all Zinbiel algebras possess a deep characteristic - they are solvable, which means they can be broken down into simpler, solvable components. This discovery has further implications, revealing that Zinbiel algebras are also nilsemisimple, and can be decomposed from semidirect sums of nil and solvable algebras.

Our analysis of one-dimensional and two-dimensional flow coefficients, derived from Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC with an energy of 5.02 TeV, builds on earlier findings for lower energies. We utilized a new VP model, incorporating hydrodynamic simulations and relativistic phase-space calculations, to compare and validate our results with experimental data collected by the ALICE detector.

In 2001, Lemmon and Macpherson introduced a specific class of dual lattices, known as split-split algebras, and demonstrated that any such algebra can be represented as a structure consisting of clopen sets within a specific type of topological space, of rank n for some positive integer n. Since then, researchers have been interested in extending this result to other classes of logics, which require a more general form of these split-algezas, and their corresponding properties, including monolithic and $\alpha$-monolithic logics, introduced by Jipsen in 2007. This paper presents the concept of unified logics, which encompass all the previously mentioned logics, and provides a necessary and sufficient condition, along with a definition of a new class of algezas, which can be used to replicate the behavior of any unified logic of a specific rank, n for some positive integer n. Additionally, this paper describes the properties of these new algezas, and proves a replication theorem for all unified logics, which states that any such logic is equivalent to a class of structures consisting of clopen sets within a space of dimension n, for some positive integer n.

Deterministic functional dependencies are a fundamental concept in database theory with wide-ranging applications. Despite their importance, existing approaches fall short in handling deterministic relations that contain missing values, a common occurrence in real-world data. Whether previous methods, such as partial functions and subfunctional dependencies, truly address the nuances of dealing with tables with nulls is questionable. This paper critically examines these approaches and introduces a unifying framework to analyze and compare them. Furthermore, we investigate the complexities associated with computing minimal deterministic functions for relations that contain missing values. Our research reveals that while this problem is computationally tractable in most cases, it becomes infeasible with 3-column deterministic relations.

Existing tools for analyzing time series with count data are limited, particularly in addressing seasonal patterns. To fill this gap, we created a novel model called the Temporal-Varying Poisson Autoregressive model, or TVPAR(p), which can handle multiple seasons. We developed theoretical properties for TVPAR(p) and conducted simulations to demonstrate its consistency, convergence, and ability to estimate seasonal parameters accurately. When compared to an alternative method, our model outperformed it in terms of estimation accuracy and bias reduction, according to both simulation and real-world data studies.

This paper introduces Neural Description Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation method, to address robustness issues when 3D objects are exposed to 3D Euclidean transformations. Unlike previous approaches that represent objects in canonical coordinates, NDFs describe the relationship between spatial positions and probability densities of locations inside target objects. By leveraging this framework, we develop techniques for 3D object manipulation, spatial reasoning, and language-guided tasks. Our model's ability to accept object poses as input ensures consistent output during dynamic scenes and multi-object interactions. We demonstrate NDFs' effectiveness in object rotation, simulation of dynamic environments, spatial reasoning, and the generation of objects from natural language.

The concept of the SiD Sensor has been widely discussed and studied for the potential construction of the ILC. Furthermore, it is being considered for possible adaptation to other linear colliders such as CLIC and CLI. This modification examines how increasing the SiD Sensor's granularity to 0.8cm x 0.8cm and reducing its total detection radius to 35cm would impact performance, particularly in relation to 3-lepton event reconstruction at the jet level and impact on inner detector other components like support structures, cooling systems, and trace detectors. This study also compares its results to using 1.2cm x 1.2cm sensors at a larger detection radius of 40cm.

We examined the spatial distribution and motion of stars in the Tonantzintla 2 open cluster using a comprehensive spectral analysis. We investigated 39 galaxies within the cluster, specifically focusing on their NPVs. By combining this data with existing catalogues, we created a 3D model of the cluster. Our analysis revealed that the cluster has a scattered spatial distribution, with a scale length of 3.4 kPc in the galactic plane. The cluster primarily consists of metal-rich stars, with a gradient in spectral characteristics as you move away from the galactic center. Additionally, we found the cluster to be dynamically hot. Our findings suggest that the cluster is not formed of a coherent ring, but rather a dispersed group of stellar material.

The proliferation of verified components in the Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs (Isabelle AFP) has fostered a robust framework for VDL development. However, the complex structure of the AFP has made navigating and extending this framework challenging for researchers and engineers. This report introduces a set of criteria to assess and evaluate demonstration frameworks within specific domains, subsequently, we analyze and refine the current Isabelle VDL demonstration framework, addressing identified areas of concern, and propose potential enhancements, all detailed findings are available online at https://github.com/hjdwang/isabelle-bench.

This study explores how the Yang-Lee edge criticality (YLEC) fits within traditional order-disorder transition frameworks of spin systems, specifically in the context of O(N) universality classes. Research indicates that in models with N≥3, the YLEC properties align with those of a diagonal transition, and further analysis reveals the presence of 'critical zeros' of polyadic equations on the unit circle for these N≥3, even though they have no impact on the dominant zero pattern that defines the system's critical behavior.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a optimization algorithm is working within a region of interest that has convex properties. Our research makes two key contributions: first, we provide an innovative proof of the local concavity of the TAP free energy function, which is critical for proving that the message passing algorithm converges to a globally optimal solution. Secondly, we develop an iteration-based technique to demonstrate that regions reachable via successful iterations of the asymptotic message passing algorithm lie within a region of interest with desired properties. This technique yields several benefits: it enables an efficient representation of the set of reachable solutions, it provides a straightforward proof of the local concavity of the TAP free energy function, and it offers insights into the behavior of the message passing algorithm in random k-sat problems and random matrix multiplication, demonstrating in particular that for random k-sat with density below a threshold, two distinct regions of accessibility emerge.

This educational manuscript offers a comprehensive examination of metasurfaces, cutting-edge materials featuring an ultra-thin thickness. It entails an examination of fundamental concepts, among them transmission-line models and effective medium approximations, as well as periodic resonant structures, within a computational framework. By making use of readily available computational electromagnetic modeling tools, we explore the capacity of these advanced materials to manipulate wave propagation in both transmission-line and volumetric contexts.

The primary objective of this research is to establish the feasibility of approximating a smooth, fully integrable vector field with a given non-degenerate periodic orbit by a vector field that has a specific orbital equivalence. To achieve this, we have developed a method of construction for the desired integrable vector field. Additionally, a key consequence of this result is the confirmation of the local orbital linearization theorem for specific nonlinear periodic orbits.

Although the configuration interaction method yields precise solutions to the electronic Schrodinger equation, its extensive computational demands restrict its use to simple molecular systems. To overcome this limitation, a new deep schrodinger equation solver is proposed. This model consists of three key components: a cyano unit that quartically parametres nuclear coordinates; a ci unit that quadratically parametres the electronic coordinates; and a linear unit that bridges the two units. Notably, despite the limited capacity of the ci unit, the proposed model is capable of quadratically scaling computational costs for molecular schrodinger energy calculations. As a result, it can accurately predict CI energies across a wide range of test systems.

The discovery of massive separations between intrinsically massive galaxies and their companion low-mass satellites has been observed in local clusters, yet these massive distances were unaccounted for until recently. Our new observations of galaxies in the Coma cluster have revealed these companions are significantly separated from their primary galaxies. These low-mass satellites were found to be widely dispersed, with some located over 1.5 million parsecs away from their primary companions. The likelihood of this occurring by chance is extremely low, with a probability of only 0.3% when considering the typical separation patterns of galaxies in the Coma cluster. Our findings suggest the existence of massive gravitational connections between these galaxies, which is also reflected in their color and magnitude differences.

The precision of photometric and astrometric data from ground-based telescopes is being utilized to improve our understanding of atmospheric conditions, specifically the composition of scattering agents in the Earth's atmosphere. A key aspect of this investigation involves the development of new, effective methods for the continuous and accurate measurement of aerosol properties across a wide area. This study makes original contributions to the field of aerosol research by suggesting innovative approaches to modeling the atmospheric transmission curve through the combination of photometric information and the atmospheric transmission curve.

This paper proposes a novel DeepHMap++ approach for pose estimation that builds upon our previous work, utilizing a 6-degree-of-freference pose space, in contrast to the conventional 5-degree-of-freence pose representation. We incorporate a DeepHMap predictor, which projects poses onto the 6DoF space and employs a correspondence learning module to extract hierarchical cosine maps, effectively capturing the correspondence relationships between poses and their respective projections. To enhance pose estimation performance, we introduce a novel clustering method called merged projection clustering, which clusters the cosine maps by first merging the projection results from adjacent poses. This innovation leads to a substantial improvement of 4.27% in mean average error compared to our previous approach.

Nonlocal integral models have gained significant attention in recent years due to their ability to accurately describe and predict complex phenomena that occur in materials under extreme stress, causing irreversible changes. This interest in nonlocal models has also been driven by a better mathematical and physical comprehension of their underlying principles, as opposed to their predecessors, which had limited range of applicability. This review introduces a novel class of nonlocal elasticity theories, called bond-oriented peridynamics, and examines their role in the nonlocal analysis of fluids and their surrounding materials. It discusses various bond-oriented peridynamic theories, including their definitions, constitutive equations, and the methods used to solve their governing equations. The review also explores the application of these theories to fluid mechanics and coupled multiphysics problems, highlighting their potential for addressing highly nonlinear and complex problems that challenge traditional models.

Graphical Lasso is an established technique for estimating a precision matrix, but Generalized Graphical Lasso, a more advanced variant, poses computational challenges due its non-linear constraints. This issue can be exacerbated in large-scale computations and high-dimensional scenarios. A novel Generalized Graphical Lasso implementation in Python is now available through a new open-source package, GGLasso, which leverages existing convex optimization tools to efficiently solve the problem.

Numerous simulations modeling molecular dynamics and polymers rely on simulations of particles interacting through deterministic stochastic Langevin dynamics, providing them with configurational sampling methods. Despite advancements, configuring these simulations remains challenging due to their inherent complexity. In these simulations, each molecular component experiences resistance proportional to its velocity due to an implicit numerical method. Deterministic treatment of this friction leads to smooth, continuous trajectories for the involved degrees of freedom. In contrast, traditional stochastic simulation techniques model random numerical forces arising from the interaction, which can result in unrealistic and erratic behavior in simulations of complex molecular structures. This study reveals that this apparent improvement in simulation accuracy comes at the cost of increased numerical instability, which manifests especially in molecular structures. This discovery leads us to propose a novel simulation approach, which determines the optimal balance between numerical stability and efficiency in molecular simulations, achieving up to an eight-fold increase in performance while maintaining stability in molecular structures, demonstrating substantial benefits over existing methods in terms of robustness and efficiency in molecular simulations.

This research builds upon a previously developed hydrodynamic simulation model that accounts for gravitational radiation's influence, specifically "wave shadows," during the merger of two compact astrophysical objects. The original formulation was limited to describing the behavior of a gas that follows basic principles of mass conservation, energy conservation, and entropy increase. The merger of two such systems, whether they are two black holes, neutron stars, or any other type of compact object, may produce compelling multimessenger signals. However, the impact of wave shadows on the complex interplay between general relativity's global effects and the local conservation laws of fluid systems has thus far remained unexplored. In this study, we expand the previous model to better understand how the merger of two systems affects their surrounding environments, taking into account the influence of black holes' event horizons on the remaining matter. We employ an effective viscosity that mimics the absorption of the black holes as well as a generalized smoothing length to accurately prevent the accumulation of matter beyond a certain distance, analogous to the photon ring seen in simulations of the Event Horizon Telescope's observation of G2.0. The resulting model allows us to replicate the striking ring seen in the emission from gas that merges around a black hole, as well as a range of new scenarios where the interplay between the objects and their surrounding environments gives rise to rich and dynamic multimessenger signals.

Consider an extended Euler-Bernoulli beam consisting of four sub-beams connected at their endpoints and resting on a star-shaped foundation. We analyze the uniform stability of this system when equipped with rotational inertia at the inner vertex and resistant dampers at its outer spans. Utilizing a combination of an auxiliary function and a common Lyapunov function, a key proportion is derived linking the bending stiffnesss of the inner sub-beams to that of the outer sub-beams. This derivation enables demonstration that all eigenvalues of the associated operator are located in the right half of the complex plane, and ultimately, through a second derived proportion, system stability is shown.

Researchers have developed a groundbreaking acoustic lens material based on P(VDF-HFP) that effectively enhances acoustic detection systems, addressing the limitation of current detection systems which lose 30-40% of acoustic energy. This novel formulation exhibits improved properties including lower density, better chemical stability, and a significantly reduced acoustic impedance. Specifically, the lens material increases the acoustic energy reaching detectors by 40-50%. Through numerical simulations and experimental verifications, the research demonstrates the material's ability to acoustic focus and evenly distribute acoustic energy across detection areas. The study also shows the potential for this material to improve the image quality and reduce image artifacts in photoacoustic breast imaging, a critical application for the technology.

Community detection and node classification are fundamental problems in the fields of network analysis and machine learning. Current prominent methods, such as the prominence method developed by Boldi and Villa, effectively address the issue of ranking nodes within a singular network. However, these methods fall short of accuracy and applicability in networks that consist of multiple layers. Before utilizing prominence methods in multilayer networks, a critical assessment of their limitations in such environments is necessitated. Our study utilizes multilayer networks that exhibit prominent community structures as test subjects to explore the potential of the prominence method. Initially, we employ the prominent layers to form distinct community structures and evaluate its effectiveness. Subsequently, we investigate the prominence method's performance in networks characterized by dependent node importance. Our findings indicate that while the prominence method can successfully identify clear community structures in multilayer networks, its accuracy declines when dealing with ambiguous structures, thus suggesting its current suitability for practical application. Moreover, our research demonstrates that certain parts of the local prominence features possess enhanced community-detecting capabilities, leading to the potential of utilizing only the most significant portions of these features. Our findings also reveal a near 10% improvement in precision-at-top-100 and a 20% reduction in running time, when utilizing the most significant portions of these features. Ultimately, our study contributes to the critical assessment of the prominence method within multilayer networks and proposes a novel, reliable approach for community detection.

Our research suggests that a single neural network can effectively handle multiple degradation tasks, such as demosaicing, deblurring, and denoising, even when they occur simultaneously in sensor data. To test this hypothesis, we created four intricate synthetic datasets and a real one, in which we controlled the deformation processes. We then evaluated our single-model approach against a collaborative model of specialized networks and found that it matches or exceeds their performance. Notably, our findings reveal that pre-training is crucial for realistic scenarios and that a single network is nearly as effective as an ideal specialized network. This indicates that there's minimal loss when replacing multiple collaborative specialists with a single generalist.

This project introduces the Causal Exploration Toolbox (CEX), a set of advanced techniques and relevant frameworks for exploring and inferring causality in data, with a focus on work conducted in economics and operations management. By leveraging the causal inference module in Python (PyIcau), CEX streamlines the process of studying the causal effects of variables and can be integrated into educational settings, research, and professional applications. As an extension to PyIcau, CEX provides additional methods for exploring and uncovering causality, with features such as the do operator, counterfactual analysis, Bayesian networks, and discovery techniques, all with an emphasis on education.

A study is conducted to understand how nonporous spheres act when they come into contact with fluid, 
specifically in a resting state or in motion within the fluid, and how this leads to a surface seal, 
known as "liquid entry surface sealing," which traps air above the sphere and creates a complex 
fluid dynamics system surrounding it. 
To further this understanding, researchers examined a range of conditions involving spheres moving 
through static fluid and found that a new range, or "gap," has been identified where liquid entry 
surface sealing frequently happens. This range was previously difficult to predict theoretically 
and had not been adequately addressed by existing models. 
The study fills this gap by presenting the first comprehensive assessment of the boundary between 
when the seal forms and when it does not, based on a series of experiments and statistical 
analysis. 
Additionally, the study shows that, in most cases, sealing occurs within defined thresholds at 
both the beginning and end of this newly identified gap.

In a well-studied class of four-dimensional Type IIB string theory effective theories, we investigate unbroken supersymmetry conditions for generic axio-dilaton and Kalb-Ramond field values. An key aim is to identify nontrivial global symmetries that could exist. Our analysis reveals the potential for a new type of EFT $\theta$-term, distinct from previously known terms, arising from D3-instantons within this scenario. Another significant finding is that, for certain boundary conditions, it is possible to break all global symmetries, an extreme case of vacuum structure. We, however, focus on the more common scenario of partial symmetry breaking and explore its implications. To understand the dynamics of this case, we simplify boundary conditions, thereby facilitating further study of potential consequences, such as those related to the cosmological constant.

Confidential computing systems, which employ trusted hardware to process sensitive data, are vulnerable to confidence attacks that undermine public skepticism. As a result, security practitioners have started focusing on maintaining transparency. However, current methods either rely on unproven cryptographic techniques or impose significant performance penalties. In contrast, our objective is to minimize confidence attacks in physically isolated environments without using heavy assumptions. We discovered that the degree of public oversight directly impacts a attacker's incentive to hack these systems. Therefore, we developed two innovative, lightweight techniques – Configuration Locking and Monitoring, and Locking and Recording and Replaying. These techniques ensure that users and a attacker can verify the absence of malicious activity, providing valuable insights into the attacker's potential gains. Notably, Configuration Locking and Monitoring achieves a 5x reduction in potential public oversight costs compared to relying solely on Confidometrics.

Machine learning models are vulnerable to modeling errors and malicious attacks, 
which can result in substantial performance losses and reliable classifier manipulation. 
To address robust classification, a new optimization framework is needed that can 
reliably optimize the difference between the true and predicted distributions. 
However, calculating the true distribution is not feasible. 
In this paper, we introduce a novel approach that combines a non-convex optimization method 
with a theory of resilient policy gradient to achieve resilient policy optimization. 
We mathematically prove our method's ability to produce reliable solutions under certain conditions. 
To overcome optimization challenges, we modify the original framework and propose an efficient algorithm. 
To assess the robustness of our method, we conducted experiments on real-world datasets and common defense techniques. 
The results show our method significantly outperforms existing approaches and achieves a 10-to-1 improvement over standard techniques, 
demonstrating an average 3.3-times enhancement compared to them.

We introduce an exclusive category of players in a well-known economic experiment,  
which surprisingly leads to an unexpected outcome, even more so given the  
players' past success in a similar situation. Moreover, in this specific  
context, exclusive players seem to evoke reciprocal behavior from others, a  
phenomenon that doesn't appear in the comparable situation. These results,  
however, seem to contradict previous research, indicating the critical importance  
of framing effects.

Cubanite $CuFe_2S_3$ exhibits magnetic ordering with a type-N pattern, exhibiting an Neel temperature of 18K, while displaying nonmagnetic, semiconducting properties.  Our calculations show that semiconducting behavior can arise from strong correlations in the $3d$ shell of Fe, while a mean-field approach predicts metallic results.  By incorporating Hubbard $U$ self-energy, our method yields strong orbital selectivity, resulting in occupied $t_{2g}$ bands for $e_g$.  This strong selectivity matches experimental capacitive measurements.  Our GGA+$L$-self-energy method predicts an insulating gap within the $t_{2g}$ manifold, while the $e_g$ group exhibits a small overlap.  Strong strong orbital selectivity within cubanite distinguishes it from other $3d$ semiconductors.  Within the $t_{2g}$ manifold, cubanite exhibits Mott-$t_{2g}$ insulating behavior akin to $Sc_2O_3$.  The $e_g$ group exhibits Mott-$t_{2g}$ insulating characteristics similar to $LaMnO_3$. A substantial external magnetic field is typically needed to achieve Dark Exciton (DE) oscillations, but this requirement poses a challenge as it demands excessively high costs and affects the optical purities required for practical applications. Notably, our calculated results indicate that, due to the presence of massive Rabi oscillations, a significant Rabi frequency associated with LIEEx can facilitate effective LIEEx to Bright Exciton (BEx) conversion even in the absence of an external magnetic field. Based on this, our research proposes utilizing a large Dark Exciton proportion provided by electron-hole mass asymmetry to establish a reliable and efficient quantum source based on the LIEEx state, which can be converted to the BEx state through a moderate external magnetic field.

Within the 11 non-equivalent non-symmorphic wallpaper groups, particularly those with glide symmetries, a lattice exists that incorporates additional electronic bands beyond the standard six-fold symmetry. Recent computational analysis using tight-binding models is being applied to investigate the potential for Dirac points within each of these groups. We have identified two groups, cgg and pgg, that can host Dirac points at specific high-symmetry k-points, allowing for a two-dimensional lattice composed of non-interacting dimer molecules. By adjusting a control variable in this lattice, we can manipulate the positions of Dirac points. Furthermore, it is possible to achieve a non-Abelian anyon Berry phase, an anomalous winding number, and a anomalous Hofstadter butterfly in this lattice.

A novel type of quantum state known as single-photon facilitated coherent states (SFCS) can be created effectively using quantum-optical catalysis. In experiment, a beam splitter is used to combine a weakly illuminated input with an intensely illuminated local oscillator. However, this method isn't feasible in practice due to the requirement for precise photon detection and lack of Phased Space multiplexing. To overcome this, we developed a new, achievable process where the intensity-modulated local oscillator interacts with the weakly illuminated signal over an extremely short interaction time with a nonlinear optical crystal, yielding high-fidelity SFCS even with sub-optimal equipment. These states can also be transformed into entangled multi-mode states by sharing the quantum information with multiple identical spatial modes, which has the potential to enhance optical communication capacity. Our research demonstrates that optical super-catalysis can detect and analyze complex entangled states like Gaussian multi-mode states.

We transform the 10 Einstein field equations from the Newman-Penrose (NP) formalism, which utilizes a null tetrad basis, into algebraic equations for the electromagnetic bivectors formed by complex combinations of complex conjugate Fij, where FiJ represents the Riemann tensor. This transformation specifically focuses on separating the complex self-dual and anti-self-dual parts of the Weyl curvature Bivectors Cij. By applying the NP formalism to both Einstein-Maxwell and Weyl gravity theories, we evaluate how the null tetrad basis responds to the separation of these components. As a result, the 4 complex equations for the electromagnetic bivectors are further simplified to 2 complex equations for massless photon fields when expressed in the Hamiltonian language with respect to null Lorentzian coordinates, and similarly, the 4 complex equations for the Weyl curvature bivectors reduce to 2 complex equations for spacetime null coordinates.

Finding efficient transport methods for complex molecular structures is a major challenge in chemistry. Recent research has proposed using linear regression and whole programming to analyze and deduce the structural characteristics of chemicals from their spectroscopic data. This study further explores this approach by demonstrating its potential for researching polymers, using polystyrene as a case study. Results show that the method successfully determined the polymer's monomer unit, molecular weight distribution, and key parameters, including the peak, average, and width of its GPC graph.

This paper introduces an immediate transcription method that can provide real-time, dynamic harmonization and timbre enhancement for breathing sounds. Additionally, it proposes an innovative application for these sounds in a non-liturgical context, and presents an example that explores their use.

A 3D CT image is broken down into 2D slices for easier processing and visualization. Each slice represents a cross-section of the object at a specific point along its length. However, this division can lead to the loss of vital information, making it challenging to visualize and analyze the object in three dimensions. Despite this difficulty, many medical images are captured in this format, as 2D CT scans offer a balance of safety, ease of use, and accuracy, offering a well-established baseline for computer-assisted diagnosis systems.

One important application of computer-assisted diagnosis is the accurate detection and identification of tumors, including their differentiation from non-cancerous tissue. While radiologists can accurately diagnose tumors based on years of experience, the high cost of training and the subjective nature of human decision-making drive the need for the development of advanced computer systems capable of performing these tasks with greater efficiency. Although existing methods for image segmentation have shown promise, they often struggle with accurately identifying boundaries and producing leaky segments. To address these limitations, researchers have developed the Dilated Dense Dense Unet (DDAUnet) model, which leverages both global context and surface details to improve image segmentation accuracy, outperforming traditional techniques like 3D Dense Unet and regular Unet.

Our system employs a novel, 1D approach using an 11-element aggregate model to interpret log measurements, providing a straightforward yet versatile framework for geologists and engineers to assess formation properties like porosity, saturation, and rock density. In contrast to more intricate methods, our model offers an additional benefit of calculating uncertainties in formation parameter estimates by integrating probabilistic error propagation, essential for geologists to evaluate risks and make informed decisions during the geosteering process. Geosteering is crucial for maintaining well trajectories within reservoirs, leveraging real-time logging measurements to guide drilling processes, but its success relies on the accuracy of downhole tool data, necessitating careful assessment of uncertainties in geological parameters.

Nested named entity recognition, a challenge where some entities contain others, is prominent in domain-specific information extraction tasks and lacks sufficient study in NLP. We reframe nested named entity detection as identifying hierarchical structures within documents, rather than just recognizing individual entities. Taking this structural perspective, we propose Holistic Nested Entity Detection (HoLED), a method that employs graph neural networks to analyze the full document hierarchy. Our results show HoLED outperforms current best practices on three evaluation datasets, achieving significant performance gains of 2.85 F-score on Wikipedia CC-NER, 2.46 on PubMed, and 1.75 on BioAdversarial.

We'll examine the connection between rational and tropical hypersurfaces of a specific complex quartic surface, and its impact on the calculation of bitangent planes to that surface. A corresponding tropical problem is shown to have a fully describable set of solutions to its rational counterpart, and the A^1-count of those bitangent planes is proven to equal the count of bitangent planes to the underlying quartic surface over the real numbers.

This research focuses on the 2D trilateration method for locating targets within a sensor network. To enhance the accuracy of trilateration, researchers have developed a technique to mitigate the errors caused by cross-technology disruption in proximity to transmitting sensors. A listener is created using opcodes from the 802.15.4 protocol to record the time of arrival and signal strength from both IEEE 802.15.4 and IEEE 802.11 protocol transmissions. Based on previous research, an empirical mathematical model is created to calculate the distance between the transmitting node and the listening sensor, utilizing parameters obtained from the time of arrival, signal strength, and frequency of transmitted and receiving sensors. To test the effectiveness of the proposed technique, the opcodes are implemented on the 15.4 sensor, and the distance estimation results are compared to actual measurements using a computer-controlled system.

This paper outlines key challenges and considerations for developing an effective code-mixed Natural Language Processing, highlighting the necessity of addressing language disparities while improving overall accessibility for multilingual users.

Evaluating the accuracy of generated text, particularly in the context of image descriptions, is commonly done through comparison with human-written references. Unfortunately, this method is hindered by the fact that human-written references can contain errors, are often modified for the sake of relevance but may no longer accurately reflect the original meaning, and are typically created by multiple people, making them ideal references for evaluation scarce. This paper aims to investigate the effectiveness of using human-generated data as ideal references for assessing automatic image descriptions. We conducted a study where we assessed the performance of different evaluation metrics combined with ideal references in six languages, employing three datasets in four of those languages. As a result, our research confirms that ideal references derived from human-written text perform significantly better than standard references in terms of precision, recall, and F1 scores. This finding is corroborated by our data, which shows that ideal references achieve an average improvement of 17.7% across all evaluation metrics.

Our study determines the most stable crystal structure of Ta$_2$O$_5$ by comparing various configurations. We calculate the free energy of 14 different arrangements, considering Ta and O atoms swapping their positions, and 8 additional configurations to validate our results. VASP was used to calculate the electronic ground state, and a Monte Carlo simulation with SWAP-enabled density functional theory determined the best arrangements at temperatures between 0K and 3000K. As a result, our study finds the monoclinic C2 space group to be the most stable configuration of Ta$_2$O$_5$ at temperatures up to 160K.

Geographic distribution significantly impacts how information spreads within online communities. With the rise of social media platforms, these accounts can quickly amplify both accurate and inaccurate news. This research focuses on Reddit users to analyze the role of a large-scale geographic separation on the spread of fake news. A data set consisting of 3.4 million comments from r/fakenews between 2015 to 2019 was examined to explore this relationship. A combination of a geographic network model and entropy-based method was used to measure the geographic distribution of Redditors posting fake news and uncover its evolution over time and associated patterns. The results showed that fake news generally surpasses real news in terms of reach but also confirmed that Redditors who engage with both genuine and fabricated stories are often concentrated in the same regions. Furthermore, certain states with substantial Redditor populations tend to be more susceptible to fake news. Notably, r/fakenews participants located in the Northeast region of the U.S. have a higher tendency to share fake news with a wider audience. These findings can inform the design of online platforms to limit the spread of fake news.

Humans frequently employ gestures and language when teaching skills to others. Research has shown that speakers are capable of conveying precise spatial information to listeners using natural language, consistently outperforming models lacking this verbal input. No study has yet examined how human instructors use language when demonstrating tasks to robots in a physical setting. This research involves recording sessions of human experts practicing assembly and insertion tasks alongside nine university students who are teaching the same tasks to a robot. These recordings include the instructors' verbal instructions, which are then analyzed through statistical methods to reveal the acoustic characteristics of effective instructors. Furthermore, we have trained a classifier that can accurately predict the effective experts based on the paralinguistic features of their verbal communication, achieving a accuracy of above 0.8.

The topology of Random Critical Galton-Watson (RCGW) trees has long been studied, 
with recent findings indicating their statistical similarity to Limiting Poisson 
two-dimensional (LP2) trees. 
However, both RCGW and LP2 models are limited to a single type of structure, 
whereas many real-world examples exhibit greater structural diversity. 
In response, we introduce a more flexible model that accommodates a variety of 
probability distributions, 
and demonstrate that this new model also shares the properties outlined in Theorem 1. 
Furthermore, we establish additional distinctions between the new model, 
RCGW, LP2, and their respective underlying probability distributions. 
To achieve this, we employ both analytical methods, 
specifically generating functions, as well as numerical simulations to validate 
our findings.

Our research reveals a complex relationship within the world of Euler-Arnold equations, connecting features of gauge theory from physics to the algebra of differential operators. A specific differential equation, solvable under particular conditions, reveals an unexpected property where non-commuting operators can be transformed into a form that reflects differential properties. Furthermore, this complex relationship arises from a deeper, hidden symmetry discovered through a novel, geometric interpretation of field theory.

The concept of a chatbot has been around for nearly four decades, and currently, they serve in over 200 languages, offering assistance in areas from customer service to business support, and even companionship. Given the varied purposes of chatbots, assessing their effectiveness becomes a complex task. Existing evaluation methods for conversational agents depend heavily on user input, making them inflexible, and current benchmarks for specific applications lack generalizability. To address these shortcomings, we have developed a comprehensive framework that provides 10 diverse scenarios for testing chatbots, assessing their ability in essential functions such as information exchange, problem solving, task management, human-like conversation, emotional support, advice, problem solving, human-like conversation, and social interaction, along with basic human capabilities. This framework is easily adaptable to new use cases, enabling seamless integration of custom evaluation metrics through a modular design. We have also showcased the framework's capabilities by assessing several state-of-the-art chatbots.

Our methodology involves strategically placing virtual objects, called Planet X's, in various positions within the unseen beyond-Planet X region. Subsequently, we use the data provided by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory's Horizons system to analyze the residual errors in the trajectories of the known planets. The analysis of these residual errors is carried out within a 3D space map, specifically focusing on the region between Planet X and the orbit of Neptune. The discovery of local anomalies in the data, particularly those aligned with the position of Planet X and located in the inner part of this region, supports the hypothesis of the existence of as-yet undiscovered massive objects within the solar system's outer boundaries. Notably, the mass of these objects is estimated to be at least $5$ times that of the Earth.

Previous work on monolingual translation archive has showcased its potential to enhance monolingual text-based tasks. To further investigate, the authors introduce a novel multilingual translation archive that encompasses both monolingual and cross-lingual translations, enabling them to extend the archive's benefits to multilingual translation. They employ multilingual translation archive multilingual translation task as the primary evaluation, though it can also be utilized to supplement other multilingual NLP tasks. To tackle the challenge of incorporating low-resource languages, they propose the concept of neural machine rendering, which allows for the combination of translations from multiple monolingual sources. They developed a simple yet effective framework for neural machine rendering, incorporating the technique of contrastive loss to ensure high-quality translations. The proposed method significantly surpasses strong baseline approaches. Notably, the multilingual translation archive they created, encompassing 49 languages, along with the neural machine rendering technique, will be made publicly available.

Researchers have proposed using the patterns of the cosmic microwave background to search for evidence of pre-big bang events, specifically a "cyclical" history. However, the current theoretical predictions and statistical methods used to analyze the data do not fully account for the impact of inflation on the patterns of the cosmic microwave background. We have developed an expanded version of the cyclical model that includes pre-big bang signals and introduced a method to statistically test for the significance of these signals. When applied to analysis using 10 years of Planck data, the results indicate that some unusual features, such as the lack of large-scale fluctuations, a specific pattern of temperature changes, and a concentrated area of polarization, may be signatures from the pre-big bang era, but these findings are heavily influenced by random variations.

This study introduces methods to establish convergence of the Yamabe flow, a dynamic version of the Yamabe flow, within certain initial data categories associated with a lower bound on the scalar Yamabe curvature. Building on previous research, this condition is less restrictive than the requirement for bounded Yamabe factors, allowing for potential expansion to include scenarios where the conformal factor grows exponentially. Additionally, the established convergence outcomes are applied to demonstrate the existence of stationary solutions within the flow.

To efficiently adapt to new tools and techniques, humans can quickly categorize information when presented with minimal examples, a skill known as few-shot learning. This capability can be harnessed to reduce the amount of training data needed for various tasks. However, current methods struggle to replicate the easy generalization humans exhibit from minimal samples. This research proposes a simple yet effective approach to enhance generalization from minimal samples by creating prototypes that represent an entire class, using data from throughout the data distribution. We examine the proposed method's results, comparing it against other established methods.

Cross-domain recommendation has emerged as a promising method to address the cold-start problem in new domains and offer a more diverse set of suggestions. However, current single Thorough Aspect Preference Learning (TAPR) techniques face two key challenges: first, they only consider individual preferences and ignore the interconnections between aspects within each item; second, they treat all domains with equal importance, disregarding the varying relevance of each domain to a target item. To address these issues, we introduce a multi-sparse-domain cooperative recommendation technique based on enhanced TAPR, which is composed of three primary components. Firstly, we incorporate pairwise Thorough Aspect Preference Learning (TAPR) to capture the complex relationships within each item; secondly, we use a multi-task preference learning framework that dynamically allocates more relevant domains to each item; and thirdly, we use a multi-sparse-domain adaptive learning framework to handle the varying availability of data from different domains. Through these components, our method is able to leverage the complementary information available in multiple domains to improve recommendation performance. We conducted numerous experiments to validate the effectiveness of our proposed technique, which yielded state-of-the-art results on the dataset used.

Organic conic optimization represents an innovative method of expressing and solving complex optimization problems by leveraging standard convex optimization frameworks. However, most existing organic conic solvers rely on second-order cone (SOC) or positive semidefinite (PSD) blocks, which can unnecessarily complicate the process. Our experience with Hypatia.jl, a newly developed organic conic formulation and solving toolkit, reveals that direct conversion of a solver's interface to an organic conic format yields a more streamlined and reliable solution, particularly when dealing with over 500 conic blocks. By utilizing the Hypatia conic interface, our case study successfully converted a 35th-degree Travelling Salesman Problem into an equivalent semidefinite program, a task that was previously unachievable with traditional SOC/PSD block converters like CVX or MOSEK.

Using machine learning models trained on labeled data for medical image analysis has been extensively studied, but their performance tends to deteriorate when applied to unlabeled images, a common scenario in clinical settings. Such models can subtly signal quality problems in images that are not labeled. Can they also provide reliable predictions for images without labels? Our research reveals that model performance varies significantly based on how representative the training data is of the clinical population. To tackle this issue, we developed a novel metric to assess model generalization capabilities and found that most models struggle with true multi-class setting. Furthermore, we observe that label noise often goes undetected. As a result, standard evaluation methods for clinical use may be misleading. To enhance models' generalization, we propose enforcing a true multi-class setting through triplet sampling. Finally, we tested our findings on magnetic resonance enterography quality assessment and CT scan grading tasks.

To maintain the stability of distribution networks during disruptions, leveraging stored energy in electric vehicle batteries for local power sharing is essential. This study develops a method to enhance resilience in distribution networks by allowing private EV owners to voluntarily engage in peer-to-peer energy exchange with neighbors and the grid following a disturbance. EV owners can choose to either charge or discharge their batteries based on grid prices and neighboring supply-demand状况 in a market-driven process unaffected by central control. We utilize a multi-agent system to simulate the EV owners' decisions and identify equilibrium strategies, demonstrating through numerical analysis that this approach effectively prevents large-scale outages and minimizes energy costs.

The explosive growth of IoT and mobile devices has significantly boosted the demand for data storage, but also for updating it. To address this issue, memory persistent storage, in contrast to traditional volatile RAM, can preserve data without requiringreloading from storage media like SSDs or HDDs, despite power outages. A novel comparison follows, using an Optane DC Module, replacing RAM as secondary memory, alongside SSDs and HDDs, in identical test setups, to evaluate relative performance. Unexpectedly, results show that when used to replace RAM, the Optane DC Module delivers substantially superior data access speeds, outperforming even the fastest SSDs for large block transfers.

The concept of Meeting Scheduling considering travel time has gained significant attention in research, but lower-level traffic management remains a relatively underexplored area. This project focuses on autonomous vehicles meeting at a predetermined location and time, where traffic conditions may vary, and all participants are essential to the encounter. We devised a performance metric called the Total Sum of Travel Times and presented a solution using recurrent optimization through the application of Long Short-Term Memory networks and a multi-agent system, allowing for efficient learning of optimal traffic policies in a decentralized manner.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 using a quantum mechanical method. We performed calculations on various atomic arrangements and found that the cubic CaMn3 structure is most stable for all these materials. Experimental data shows that CmSn3 has a unique phase transition at 49.6 nm, separating it into magnetic and non-magnetic states. Our theoretical findings replicate this behavior, with the non-magnetic state being more stable than the magnetic one. Furthermore, our results suggest that the GdxCm1-xSn3 series could utilize a 4 T magnetic field to fully control the material's intrinsic electroluminescence.

According to the Standard Model of particle physics, if we consider a model where all visible matter consists of three generations of quarks and lightest neutralinos as neutralinos have the lowest supersymmetric particle, it follows that each such entity contributes approximately 8.4 x 10^-10, significantly below the required 2.4 x 10^-8 value needed to explain the observed cosmic matter-antimatter imbalance. To contribute substantial dark matter mass, one could propose the existence of additional supersymmetric partners like color triplets of quarks or heavy neutral mesons such as charmonia. Alternatively, another viable scenario involves adding new heavy particles like heavy right-handed neutrinos or heavy quarks without associated supersymmetric partners. We will examine the implications of these proposals in relation to current cosmological and experimental constraints.

We provide a partial isomorphism between the set of global minima and a specific set of B-type clusters, then establish a recurrence rule for this partial isomorphism. This recurrence rule helps us fully define the set of global minima for any B-type Coxeter group and its subgroups.

Utilizing an external database, we have estimated the lensing mass distribution behind the sky areas covered by the Pantheon dataset. By analyzing this, we discovered that the Pantheon dataset is subject to a degree of scatter induced by lensing, which is varying across the magnitude of H0, and we also obtained estimates for the average amplification over a wide range of redshifts. Furthermore, we devised a correction formula for Pantheon data, which is dependent on the magnitude of H0, and applying this correction reduces scatter to a level of approximately one arcsecond at lower redshift ranges. This degree is comparable to what is expected from photon noise, and it suggests that the current Pantheon dataset may be affected more by gravitational effects than by systematic errors.

These are the written remarks for an introduction to advanced stochastic partial differential equations, specifically those explored through probabilistic methods. A brief review of fundamental concepts from functional analysis, analytic Q-felds from probability theory, and PDE will be conducted. Subsequently, key results and intuitive explanations will be included for key models, including the stochastic heat equation, Navier-Stokes equation, stochastic Navier-Stokes equation, and wave equation.

Recent advances in two-dimensional materials have highlighted transfer printing as a route for integrating diverse material systems onto complex structures. This approach is particularly useful in the field of photonics, where it enables novel designs and configurations. This work demonstrates a significant advancement in transfer printing technology, creating a unique T-shaped hub in phosphorosilicate glass (PSG). Created from PSG, this T-hub features two distinct 2D photonic material layers bonded to it at right angles. Achieved through a precise transfer printing technique, this configuration maintains the original optical properties and structural integrity of the photonic materials. Furthermore, this innovation paves the way for a significant advancement in complex 3D photonic integration, opening up previously unexplored design opportunities.

This letter outlines several test protocols designed to evaluate the robustness of Deep Learning-based tumor detection methods in MRI imagery, against various manipulation techniques. Many studies employ Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for this purpose, yet often lack evaluation of their methods' reliability. To address this gap, we define several test conditions and corresponding strategies to assess the stability of classification outcomes in a more rigorous manner. These include using identical training and testing images, employing randomized data augmentation techniques, utilizing deconvolution to reverse processing effects, and comparing results with a control group of unprocessed original images. Our findings suggest that utilizing randomized data augmentation and neural network ensembles can enhance the consistency of classification results, while the application of inverse processing methods like deconvolution yields significantly improved performance and accuracy.

The classical approach by Bernoulli relies on generating functions to define numbers, making their computation arduous. An alternative method is presented that utilizes the algebraic properties of the generating function along with the rule of quotient to derive recursive formulas, specifically tailored for determining the 2k-valued Bernoulli numbers. Furthermore, the algebraic method can be adapted to yield degenerate 2k-valued Bernoulli numbers.

The absorption line profile in spectral profiles is central to understanding a star's atmospheric properties, critical for interpreting the Doppler time series used in radial velocity exoplanet detection. A thorough understanding of line profiles is crucial, yet influenced by changes in celestial activity that affect different parts of the stellar spectrum. To mitigate this, researchers need to choose spectral lines or collections that are less sensitive to activity fluctuations. This study is conducted with the Sun as a model, through analyzing time series of solar surface intensity and spectral line profiles during various phases of its activity cycle. A wide range of line collections are assessed for their impact on estimated velocity time series, using both non-rotating and rotating sun models. A wide range of line collections are assessed for their ability to minimize apparent velocity variations caused by changes in the solar activity cycle, lines of collections are also tested on a range of equivalent width, depth, and atmospheric layer. Both in analysis of the Sun and with stellar spectra, it is difficult to anticipate the performance of line collections based on fundamental properties such as equivalent width. A significant improvement (approx. 50%) is achieved with optimized collections compared to equally sized collections and a gain of approx. 15% is achieved with selecting collections that minimize activity fluctuations, an approach that also proves beneficial with reducing activity fluctuations in low signal-to-noise ratio spectra of red dwarf stars.

A critical challenge facing the 802.15.4 protocol remains its inability to handle time, leading to prolonged and disruptive connection acknowledgments in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN). To address this issue, existing research focuses on hierarchical scope sectoring methods that integrate both random and deterministic algorithms. However, these methods struggle with bidirectional link integrity assessment and result in uneven data transmission intervals, affecting energy efficiency. An alternative approach involves dividing the frame into three distinct parts: deterministic sector, bidirectional link integrity estimation, and random gathering periods, to minimize connection acknowledgment duration. To evaluate and enhance accuracy, a maximum likelihood method can be employed, while the optimal allocation of sector lengths seeks to maximize stability, fairness, and overall performance. Furthermore, a performance analysis utilizing Markov chains provides insights into average gathering periods, performance metrics, and anti-resonance phenomena, confirming our theoretical models and ensuring a comprehensive evaluation.

Our framework, context-object (c^2o), evaluates advanced object detectors' ability to recognize context and evaluate their contribution to detection performance by generating context-less objects. It can be integrated with any sophisticated detector that outputs object keypoints, enabling the assessment of the detector's implicit scene understanding. We can modify the detected objects based on the computed context, such as removing birds perched on backs or leashes being held, and thus evaluate the detector's intrinsic comprehension of context. Furthermore, we introduce a new dataset, the 2021 ADE20k ADE20kH (human) segmentations are used to generate context for objects in this section.

This study examines multiple indefinite Kirchhoff-type elliptic problems that involve singular potentials and Tridinger-Moser nonlinearity. By applying a critical spectrum assumption, the use of a truncation technique, and an application of the Tridinger-Moser inequality, we establish both a minimal energy solution and an energy level-indexed series of solutions.

The sum of independent random variables, whose individual outcomes depend on mutually exclusive events, can lead to an interesting phenomenon known as concentration. This paper investigates a specific scenario where the concentration disparity between two binary random variables is studied. Unlike previous work, this paper does not assume the variables are independent. Instead, it explores their relationship through concavity constraints, specifically focusing on their concentration disparity when they are independent versus when they satisfy these concavity constraints, given the same marginal probabilities. A key finding in this paper is the determination of the maximum difference in entropy between two random variables, given their marginal distributions, which arises from exploring various potential configurations of their joint distributions.

This paper investigates the transverse imbalance in the azimuthal angle of hadrons produced in SIDIS when using a longitudinally polarized proton and a transversely polarized target. We focus on this effect in the region of x and -x quasi-Bjorken variables where they are nearly equal and opposite, which is typical for two-photon processes. We find that the cos$\phi_R$ asymmetry primarily arises from the interaction of target spin with the twist-2 quark scalar current, which is a type of scalar Compton effect. Additionally, we discover that the parton distribution and fragmentation functions do not need to be chiral-odd for a non-vanishing cross-section, which is a significant distinction from the case of hadron spin asymmetry.

We discuss how Lebedinsky and Sen's work can be understood through the framework of filtered algebras, which are associated with Poisson algebras. We show that the full subcategory of these algebras is equivalent to the algebra of complex units through a specific functor. This relationship is then used to demonstrate how a similar functorial approach can be applied to derive key results from quantum field theory, including the connection between Fock spaces and de Sitter geometry.

Let Y be a symplectic subsphere within a symplectic 4-manifold (X, ω). We investigate the impact of performing a symplectic surgery, known as a -1-blowup at a point on Y, while maintaining the overall symplectic structure. We establish that the resulting modified symplectic manifold is not reachable from its original form through a reverse symplectic surgery, or a bubblebling, with the distinction that the bubblebling would violate the fundamental principle of positivity of intersection. Notably, this outcome holds true with virtually no constraints on the way the curve Y is arranged within X.

This paper introduces a Wikipedia-based entity suggestion approach that leverages the structured information on Wikipedia's infoboxes to rank potential entities for a given query. By representing the Wikipedia graph as a set of layered structures, we utilize a diagonal embedding to create a 2D layout that visually highlights entity relationships. Our method combines ranking models with visualization techniques, incorporating features from Wikipedia's page hierarchy and text content. Our results on the Yahoo! Knowledge Network dataset show that our approach outperforms baseline methods, with user studies confirming the added value of layered diagrams in identifying relevant entities.

The concept of ideal compatibility between kidney donors and recipients is discussed, and a new class of incompatible kidneys is explained. These kidneys, which do not match the recipient but can be successfully transplanted with the use of desensitization or anti-T cell therapies, are examined. Given the significant backlog of candidates waiting for a kidney transplant and the limited supply of compatible organs, the research investigates the potential of transplaining these previously excluded incompatible organs. A key question arises: if the compatibility with the recipient is not ideal, could this have key implications on the long-term success of the transplant, particularly on its durability? Through computer simulations, which model the desensitization/process of anti-T cell therapies and post-transplant care, the research attempts to assess the potential success rates of transplaining these excluded incompatible organs.

Recent advances in language understanding are being swiftly made in Language Operations, where tasks are being compared to tasks requiring a language a human knows. This study is missing from the current landscape. As the current methodology is being rapidly developed with state-of-the-art models being built upon, it's critical to evaluate the foundational components of these models' success. This study is being built to assess the role of implicit instructions that are being picked up by models from the data's noise, influencing their performance on evaluations. We've constructed a straightforward framework to quantify the role of these implicit instructions, introducing a new set of tasks known as IOBench, consisting of 11340 explicit instruction-data pairs across 11 diverse evaluation domains. We've analyzed 11 prominent models, spanning from simple to complex, spanning from 30 million to over 1.8 billion parameters. The findings reveal that parametric implicit instructions are being learned by models with parameters of 30 million and above, exceeding the role of implicit data noise. Moreover, these models are exceeding the performance of models with parameters of 300 million or above, exceeding the performance of models with explicit instructions alone. Experiments with explicit instructions that are contradicted lead to models replacing them with parametric implicit instructions. We've constructed a straightforward framework to quantify the role of these implicit instructions that are being learned, introducing a new set of tasks known as IOBench, consisting of 11340 explicit instruction-data

Previous studies suggest that text embeddings lack the capability to fully perform financial task complexities. Nevertheless, there's a critical assumption underlying these researches that standard NLP techniques can readily extract meaningful semantic information from corporate documents. We scrutinize the reliability of semantic NLP techniques in accurately capturing semantic orientation in a comprehensive corporate dataset containing nearly 20,000 company names and their corresponding 170,000 words from Loughran-McDonald's financial word list. We employ diverse classification techniques, including NLP-based methods like Loughran-McDonald's polarities, sentiment analysis, and word embeddings, to evaluate their performance in categorizing companies with semantic orientation. Our findings indicate that NLP techniques yield divergent outcomes and, on average, resemble random results in 74% of the analyzed pairs, thereby revealing the questionable accuracy of these methods in correctly identifying semantic orientation in a substantial corporate dataset.

This paper integrates multiple antennas and multiple carriers in a wireless transmission system to increase the received signal strength and efficient use of spectrum. Overall, our integration achieves more effective utilization of wireless resources. To clarify the additional gain achieved, we provide simplified system configurations, derive the optimal form of a wireless transmission system with multiple antennas and multiple carriers, and explore the optimal form of a system utilizing two transmit antennas. Furthermore, we suggest OFDM as a practical waveform design due to its ease of implementation, and provide an efficient algorithm for configuring a system with two transmit antennas.

A novel approach is introduced to tackle complex phenomena during solidification and melting processes, considering convection and latent heat effects. The method combines the level-set and embedded boundary techniques. To describe the phase change process, the level-set defines the interface while the embedded boundary technique is used for spatial discretization. A key feature of this approach is its ability to use smaller time steps than traditional methods, such as the narrow band, due to the level-set's support for discontinuities. However, this comes with the constraint that the level-set does not track the history of the interface. Instead, an alternative method is proposed to determine the frozen region by analyzing where the level-set has intersected over time. The technique is used to solve the Stefan problem and a more complex process involving melting with an initial temperature distribution. The solutions obtained demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach.

In classical logic, connectives are evaluated based on input truth values to arrive at a conclusion, yet this approach poses problems when examining the quantum interpreter language, especially with unary connectives. Research has successfully introduced quantum interpretations for the negation of statements, as well S4 modality operators, now we aim to generalize negation to any unary connection, proving the impossibility of certain connections like 'double negation elimination', and investigating 'modal collapse'. Our research will also delve into questions of 'questioning a question' and 'secret codes', using these examples to highlight the characteristics of the quantum interpreter language.

In multiplayer competitions, ensuring a game's equilibria include rationalizable strategies is a significant challenge due to the absence of elimination principles for irrational strategies among peers. Our research focuses on a group of agents with limited reasoning capabilities that aim to establish a stable, rational-exequable equilibrium. We introduce the concepts of rationalizability, a novel protocol called R-Prune, and an innovative strategy known as the Rationality Leap. The R-Prune protocol enables the agents to iteratively remove strategies, while the Leap strategy facilitates a rapid adjustment in the representation of strategies to achieve rationalizability. The results of our R-Prune experiments with the Leap strategy demonstrate that we can achieve an equilibrium that satisfies rationalizability within an acceptable timeframe for agents with limited reasoning capabilities in games with up to five players and $250$ strategies per player.

A dynamic model known as the 'rewired random graph' is used to represent the evolution of social connections over time. This graph model is extended to incorporate a feature of protective rewiring, where edges are removed to avoid the spread of an epidemic. Researchers applied a standard probabilistic analysis to the enhanced graph model, using it to study how protective rewiring affects the spread of infections. This involved comparing the size of communities formed by infected individuals to the magnitude of clusters created through the rewiring process. The analysis revealed three distinct outcomes in terms of community size in terms of almost sure community collapse, community coexistence, and community domination, depending on the degree of protective rewiring. The study found that almost sure community collapse and community domination are also applicable to the original graph model.

In this study, we examine a type of manifold called a nonholonomic Kenmotsu 3-$h$-manifold. By introducing a semi-symmetric connection with a symmetric torsion, we investigate how a Cotton connection relates to the nearby connection. We establish the necessary conditions for a connection to be a Cotton soliton, occurring when the underlying manifold has Cotton soliton properties. Furthermore, we analyze the behavior of the Cotton soliton in relation to the given connection.

The framework proposed in this study provides a systematic approach to modifying parton distribution functions, incorporating influences from heavy partons, parton-parton scattering, and dynamic effects such as spacetime flows and the expansion of the universe. A new parameterized framework is introduced to analyze and predict these influences on parton distributions within a consistent theoretical context, facilitating the exploration of novel concepts through well-defined variations in probability densities.

A common method used in learning agents that apply deep reinforcement learning to sequential decision-making tasks is combining trained models with a large collection of past data. One issue with this approach is that the experience corpus may contain varying levels of value depending on the agent's policy, which can lead to instability and slowed convergence during model training. To overcome this problem, we have developed an innovative technique to boost the consistency of past data in terms of its value, which we believe can facilitate the agent's model to more efficiently gain valuable insights and more rapidly converge to an optimal solution. To show the effectiveness of our technique, we conducted thorough experiments on several deep reinforcement learning environments, which resulted in more stable convergence and faster solution findings.

Our analysis of recent experimental data, including resonant x-ray scattering and ultra-violet x-ray photo-spectroscopy, reveals a novel superconducting state in Ba$_{2}$YCuO$_{5}$-type layers of (Ba$_{0.6}$K$_{0.4}$)Fe$_{2}$As$_{2}$, characterized by a hexagonal crystal lattice.
